# RichText

Header: `winui/ui/text/RichText.hpp`. Spec: `winui/ui/text/RichText.hpp`.

Read-only paragraphs of formatted inlines, wrapping by default, selectable, with links and highlighters. Content that doesn't fit can flow into [RichTextOverflow](#uirichtextoverflow) containers.

The content is set with [set_blocks()](#set_blocks), as Paragraphs of Inlines. Offsets, such as the selection and [TextHighlighter](../tree/text-highlighter.md) ranges, count in [plain_text()](#plain_text). Selection is on by default. The user can drag, double-click a word, triple-click a paragraph, press Ctrl+A and Ctrl+C, and use a context menu with Copy and Select All. In a spec tree it is built by [`ui::RichText`](#uirichtext).

Example: 
```cpp
auto  row      = std::make_unique<ui::StackControl>(ui::Orientation::Horizontal);
auto* rich     = row->add(std::make_unique<ui::RichTextControl>());
auto* overflow = row->add(std::make_unique<ui::RichTextOverflowControl>()); // measured after it
rich->set_blocks({
    {.inlines = {{.text = "RichText shows "}, {.text = "formatted", .weight = ui::FontWeight::Bold},
                 {.text = " paragraphs. "}, {.text = "Links", .navigate_uri = "https://example.com/"},
                 {.text = " work too."}}},
    {.inlines = {{.text = "What does not fit the block's height goes on in the overflow."}},
     .margin  = ui::Edges{.top = 12.0f}},
});
rich->set_text_alignment(ui::TextAlignment::Justify);
rich->set_width(200.0f);
rich->set_height(120.0f);
overflow->set_width(200.0f);
rich->set_overflow_target(overflow);
window.set_content(std::move(row));
```

## `ui::RichText`

Paragraphs of formatted inlines. Builds a [ui::RichTextControl](#uirichtextcontrol).

Read-only, selectable by default and wrapping by default. Content that does not fit can flow on into a [ui::RichTextOverflow](#uirichtextoverflow).

Example: 
```cpp
window.set_content(ui::RichText{
    .blocks = {
        { .inlines = { { .text = "I am a " },
                       { .text = "RichText", .weight = ui::FontWeight::Bold },
                       { .text = " with an ", .italic = true },
                       { .text = "italic run." } } },
        { .inlines = { { .text = "A second paragraph." } }, .margin = ui::Edges{.top = 8} },
    },
    .max_width = 400,
});
```

```cpp
    .text_alignment, .character_spacing, .selection_highlight_color, .foreground, .style,
    .margin, .width, .height, .min_width, .min_height, .max_width, .max_height,
    .horizontal_alignment, .vertical_alignment, .visible, .tool_tip, .accessibility,
    .on_pointer_entered, .on_pointer_exited, .on_got_focus, .on_lost_focus, .on_key_down,
    .on_wheel, .control
}
```

## `ui::RichTextOverflow`

Where a [RichText](#uirichtext)'s content continues when it does not fit. Builds a [ui::RichTextOverflowControl](#class-richtextoverflowcontrol), named by the [RichText](#uirichtext)'s [`.overflow`](#uirichtextoverflow-overflow), or by the previous [RichTextOverflow](#uirichtextoverflow)'s for a chain. It has no content of its own. It shows whatever of its source's paragraphs the previous container in the chain could not fit.

Example: 
```cpp
const std::string                 long_text = "A text longer than one column holds...";
ui::Control<ui::RichTextOverflow> more;

window.set_content(ui::HorizontalStack{
    .spacing  = 12,
    .height   = 300,
    .content  = {
        ui::RichText{ .blocks = {{ .inlines = {{ .text = long_text }} }}, .overflow = more, .width = 240 },
        ui::RichTextOverflow{ .width = 240, .control = more }, // continues where the text stops
    },
});
```

Every field, in the order a designated initializer names them:

```cpp
ui::RichTextOverflow{
    .overflow, .style, .margin, .width, .height, .min_width, .min_height, .max_width,
    .max_height, .horizontal_alignment, .vertical_alignment, .visible, .tool_tip,
    .accessibility, .on_pointer_entered, .on_pointer_exited, .on_got_focus, .on_lost_focus,
    .on_key_down, .on_wheel, .control
}
```

| --- | --- | --- | --- |

## class RichTextOverflowControl

Derives from `ui::Element`.

Shows the part of a [RichText](#uirichtext)'s content that did not fit the block or the previous overflow container, laid out at its own width. Link one with [RichTextControl::set_overflow_target()](#set_overflow_target), and chain another one with this one's [set_overflow_target()](#set_overflow_target). It has no content of its own, so an unlinked overflow is empty.

The links don't own anything. Each container is owned by the tree like any element and must be measured after the one before it. Destroying one in the chain unlinks everything after it. Selection, copying and links work here as in the [RichText](#uirichtext), on the [RichText](#uirichtext)'s own selection.

Example: 
```cpp
const std::string long_article_text = "An article longer than one column holds...";
auto  columns = std::make_unique<ui::StackControl>(ui::Orientation::Horizontal);
auto* rich    = columns->add(std::make_unique<ui::RichTextControl>());
auto* second  = columns->add(std::make_unique<ui::RichTextOverflowControl>());
auto* third   = columns->add(std::make_unique<ui::RichTextOverflowControl>());
rich->set_blocks({{.inlines = {{.text = long_article_text}}}});
const auto column = [](ui::Element* e) { e->set_width(180.0f); e->set_height(240.0f); };
column(rich);
column(second);
column(third);
rich->set_overflow_target(second);
second->set_overflow_target(third);
window.set_content(std::move(columns));
```
